To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SiO2-Imidazoline nanocapsules (SiO2–IMI) owning a special acid/ alkali dual-stimulus release behavior were synthesized by a simple modified Stöber process.

SiO2-imizadoline nanocomposites with a dual-stimuli accelerated release property can be used as key components for construction of self-healing coatings with superhydrophobic surfaces, which have great application potential in corrosion protection.

the smart nanocomposites with dual-stimuli release function can be used as key components for construction of self-healing coating with superhydrophobic surfaces, which can effectively suppress the localized corrosion of AA2024 in 0.05 M NaCl solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of self-healing coating on AA2024 with a superhydroobic surface by using SiO2-Imidazoline nanomaterials as key component.

the design and synthesis of smart nanocontainers as a new kind of “guest” components for construction of self-healing coating with superhydrophobic surfaces, which will open up a new avenue for the development of multifunctional coatings.
the development of a novel self-healing coating with superhydrophobic surfaces, which can be used as a promising protective coating for AA2024.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides a novel and effective approach for the fabrication of self-healing coating with a super-hydrophobic surface, which is a new strategy to solve corrosion problems in the future.

this study has successfully developed an effective and environmentally friendly corrosion inhibitor release system, which is a promising candidate for the construction of self-healing coatings with superhydrophobic surfaces.
the SiO2-Imidazoline@SHSC coating can effectively protect AA2024 from localized corrosion in the long term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-healing ability of SiO2 nanocomposites is mainly dependent on the dual-stimuli-responsive release of corrosion inhibitor and the superhydrophic surface.

the smart nanocomposite (SiO2-imidazole) was prepared via a facile method and then uniformly distributed into the sol-gel coating to construct a “host”- “guest” self-healing coating with a super-hydrophobic surface, and this coating exhibited excellent self-healing ability for localized corrosion of aluminium alloy, AA 2024, which is a promising candidate for practical use.

the SiO2-Imidazoline nanocapsule with dual acid/alkali stimuli-responsive property can be applied as smart nanocarriers to construct a self-healing coating with superhydrophobic surfaces for corrosion inhibition of aluminium alloy, AA 2024.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SiO2-IMA can be used as a smart nanocontainer to construct a self-healing coating with a super-hydrophobic surface, which has great potential to be used in practical applications.
the self-healing ability of SiO2-imidezoline nanocomposites is not limited to the coating system, but also applicable to the construction of superhydrophobic coatings.

the smart nanocontainers with a special acid/acid dual-stimuli accelerated-release property can be used in the construction of self-healing coating with superhydrophobic surfaces, which is an efficient and green method for corrosion prevention of metal substrates.
